==English==

===Etymology===
US American carnival slang of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Possibly from {{m|en|scamp||swindler, cheater}} or {{bor|en|ga|cam||crooked}}. Also possibly from {{cog|da|skam}}; if so, it would be a {{dbt|en|shame|sham|nocap=1|nocat=1}}.  First use appears c. 1963 in the periodical ''{{w|Time (magazine)|Time}}''. The word became common use among the US drug culture when in early 1980, after {{w|Abscam|Operation ABSCAM}}, an [[FBI]] sting operation directed at public officials, became public.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[fraudulent#Adjective|fraudulent]] or [[dishonest]] [[business deal|deal]]. A [[swindle#Noun|swindle]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:deception}}
#: {{ux|en|That marketing scheme looks like a '''scam''' to me.}}
#: {{ux|en|a '''scam''' catches most people with any sense of compassion}}
# Something that is promoted using scams.
#: {{ux|en|That new diet burger is a '''scam'''.}}
